surfaces.part: upper leaf canopy (two tiers of foliage blobs)

answer.evidence: The clump has two leaf tiers (rows 4-26) above vertical stalks (rows 27-62). The foliage is irregular blobs with highlight speckle. It has no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse width profile. The widths change irregularly (17, 21, 24, 26, then 19 in the stalk zone), so there is no ellipse. The stalks are straight vertical bands with light and dark stripes, and their tops are hidden by leaves. They show no horizontal surface. Rows 55-60 only widen into a ground and base patch. The object reads as a front elevation of a plant, with no clearly drawn top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 16 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile, against 427-567 colours and about 108 per tile in the references. That is far lower on both measures. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans green and is a dark material tone, which matches the references. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat areas. By eye, the bamboo culms show about 3-4 green steps, with a few leaf-cluster highlights at the top. This is much shallower than the 5-6 steps and the clumped, multi-green foliage of the references. The leaf canopy is small and sparse, and the stalks are fairly uniform vertical bars with little grain. It reads as a simplified, thinner piece next to the richly textured reference trees. Bamboo is a thin, sparse plant, so the per-tile density fact is not held against it alone. Even so, the limited colour variety and shallow ramps leave it visibly flatter than the references, so it does not reach the Beodeul standard.
